fullName: Basil I the Macedonian, Byzantine Emperor
fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝巴西尔一世“马其顿人”
birthPlace: Chariopolis, Theme of Macedonia, Byzantine Empire
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国马其顿军区卡里奥波利斯
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor by Michael III
events.labelCn: 由米海尔三世加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Michael III elevated Basil at Constantinople after the elimination of Caesar Bardas, making him imperial colleague before their relationship collapsed.

events.label: Participated in the overthrow and killing of Michael III
events.labelCn: 参与推翻并杀死米海尔三世
events.note: Michael III was assassinated in the palace on Basil's orders or with his direct participation, leaving Basil as sole emperor.

events.label: Became sole Byzantine emperor
events.labelCn: 成为拜占庭帝国唯一皇帝
events.note: Basil's sole reign began after Michael III's assassination and marks the conventional foundation of the Macedonian dynasty.

events.label: Crowned his son Constantine co-emperor
events.labelCn: 加冕长子君士坦丁为共治皇帝
events.note: Basil promoted his eldest son Constantine to secure a dynastic succession.

events.label: Crowned Leo co-emperor
events.labelCn: 加冕利奥为共治皇帝
events.note: Leo, the future Leo VI, was elevated as a junior emperor while still a child.

events.label: Elevated Alexander after Constantine's death
events.labelCn: 长子君士坦丁死后晋升亚历山大为共治皇帝
events.note: After the death of Basil's favored eldest son Constantine, Alexander was elevated to the imperial college; Leo remained co-emperor.

events.label: Restored Photios as patriarch
events.labelCn: 重新任命佛提乌为君士坦丁堡牧首
events.note: Basil restored Photios to the patriarchal throne after the death of Ignatios, reversing his earlier deposition.

events.label: Completed the Nea Ekklesia in the Great Palace
events.labelCn: 完成大皇宫新教堂工程
events.note: The Nea Ekklesia became one of the most important architectural statements of Basil's reign and of the Macedonian court.

events.label: Advanced the imperial legal codification later completed under Leo VI
events.labelCn: 推进后来由利奥六世完成的帝国法律编纂
events.note: Basil sponsored the Procheiron and related legal revision that laid the groundwork for the Basilika associated with his son's reign.

events.label: Died after a hunting accident
events.labelCn: 狩猎事故后去世
events.note: Basil died after being seriously injured during a hunt. Later sources embellish the episode, so the precise mechanism of death should be treated cautiously.

sourceNote: Shaun Tougher, The Reign of Leo VI and studies of the Macedonian dynasty; John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, trans. John Wortley (Cambridge); The Cambridge History of the Byzantine Empire, ch. 'After Iconoclasm (850–886)'; Prosopographie der mittelbyzantinischen Zeit; Wikipedia used as a supplementary chronology index.
notes:
Basil rose from comparatively obscure origins to become Michael III's co-emperor and then sole ruler after Michael's assassination. His accession conventionally begins the Macedonian dynasty, whose descendants or dynastic heirs dominated the throne until 1056.

Unlinked family: father: Bardas or Constantine (identity uncertain); mother: Pankalo; spouse: Maria; spouse: Eudokia Ingerina; child: Constantine, son of Basil I; child: Stephen I of Constantinople

fullName: Leo VI the Wise, Byzantine Emperor
fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝利奥六世“智者”
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor as a child
events.labelCn: 幼年被加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Basil I elevated Leo to the imperial college, establishing him as one of the dynastic heirs.

events.label: Succeeded Basil I as senior emperor
events.labelCn: 继承巴西尔一世成为主要皇帝
events.note: Leo became senior ruler after Basil I's death, while his brother Alexander remained co-emperor.

events.label: Continued and completed major legal codification
events.labelCn: 继续并完成重要法律编纂
events.note: Under Leo the great Macedonian legal compilation known as the Basilika and the emperor's Novels were brought into their mature form.

events.label: Raised Stylianos Zaoutzes to dominant court authority
events.labelCn: 提升斯蒂利阿诺斯·扎乌策斯的宫廷权势
events.note: Zaoutzes became Leo's leading minister and received the exceptional title basileopator, illustrating the personal court politics of the reign.

events.label: Entered war with Bulgaria over a commercial dispute
events.labelCn: 因商业争端与保加利亚开战
events.note: The transfer of the Bulgarian market from Constantinople to Thessaloniki helped trigger a major war with Simeon I, ending in serious Byzantine setbacks.

events.label: Suffered the sack of Thessaloniki by Leo of Tripoli
events.labelCn: 遭遇的黎波里的利奥洗劫塞萨洛尼基
events.note: A Muslim fleet under Leo of Tripoli captured and sacked Thessaloniki, one of the empire's gravest naval disasters of the reign.

events.label: Fathered Constantine VII with Zoe Karbonopsina
events.labelCn: 与佐伊·卡博诺普西娜生下君士坦丁七世
events.note: Constantine's birth supplied Leo with the long-awaited male heir but created a canonical crisis because Zoe was Leo's fourth partner.

events.label: Contracted a fourth marriage to Zoe Karbonopsina
events.labelCn: 第四次结婚，迎娶佐伊·卡博诺普西娜
events.note: The tetragamy controversy placed the emperor in conflict with Patriarch Nicholas Mystikos over the legitimacy of a fourth marriage.

events.label: Crowned Constantine VII co-emperor
events.labelCn: 加冕君士坦丁七世为共治皇帝
events.note: Leo secured his son's formal imperial status despite the continuing controversy over his parents' marriage.

events.label: Died in Constantinople
events.labelCn: 在君士坦丁堡去世
events.note: Leo died after a reign of twenty-six years; his brother Alexander became senior emperor while the child Constantine VII remained co-emperor.

sourceNote: Shaun Tougher, The Reign of Leo VI (886–912); John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, trans. John Wortley (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; P. Karlin-Hayter on Leo VI's foreign policy; Wikipedia used as supplementary chronology.
notes:
Leo VI combined court-centered government and major legal work with repeated military difficulties against Bulgaria and Muslim naval powers. His desperate need for a legitimate male heir produced the tetragamy controversy, but Constantine VII's coronation preserved the Macedonian succession.

Unlinked family: mother: Eudokia Ingerina; spouse: Theophano Martinakia; spouse: Zoe Zaoutzaina; spouse: Eudokia Baïana; spouse: Zoe Karbonopsina; child: Eudokia; child: Anna; child: Basil

birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor under Basil I
events.labelCn: 在巴西尔一世统治下被加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Alexander was elevated after the death of his older brother Constantine and remained formally co-emperor through Leo VI's reign.

events.label: Became senior emperor after Leo VI's death
events.labelCn: 利奥六世去世后成为主要皇帝
events.note: Alexander became senior emperor while his young nephew Constantine VII remained the dynastic co-emperor.

events.label: Died suddenly, leaving Constantine VII a minor
events.labelCn: 突然去世，留下未成年的君士坦丁七世
events.note: Alexander died suddenly after a reign of about thirteen months. Narrative sources connect the death with strenuous polo or drinking, but a precise medical cause cannot be established.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, ch. 'Alexander [912–913]' (Cambridge); Shaun Tougher, studies of Leo VI and the Macedonian court; Prosopographie der mittelbyzantinischen Zeit; Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Alexander spent most of his life as a nominal co-emperor and exercised independent senior power only from Leo VI's death in 912 until his own sudden death in 913. His death reopened a minority regime around Constantine VII.

Unlinked family: mother: Eudokia Ingerina

displayNameCn: 君士坦丁七世“紫衣贵族”
fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝君士坦丁七世“紫衣贵族”
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor by Leo VI
events.labelCn: 由利奥六世加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: The child Constantine was formally integrated into the imperial succession despite the controversy over Leo VI's fourth marriage.

events.label: Became the senior dynastic emperor as a minor
events.labelCn: 未成年时成为马其顿王朝的合法皇帝
events.note: After Alexander's death, Constantine remained emperor under a succession of regencies rather than exercising personal government.

events.label: Married Helena Lekapene
events.labelCn: 与海伦娜·莱卡佩娜结婚
events.note: Romanos Lekapenos married his daughter Helena to Constantine and used the alliance to institutionalize his own control of the government.

events.label: Was subordinated to Romanos I Lekapenos as senior co-emperor
events.labelCn: 在高级共治皇帝罗曼努斯一世之下被架空
events.note: Romanos I was crowned and soon took precedence over Constantine, who retained legitimacy but little practical authority.

events.label: Survived the overthrow of Romanos I by the Lekapenoi princes
events.labelCn: 在莱卡佩诺斯诸王子推翻罗曼努斯一世的危机中保住皇位
events.note: Romanos I's sons Stephen and Constantine deposed their father but failed to displace Constantine VII, whose dynastic popularity proved decisive.

events.label: Became sole effective emperor
events.labelCn: 成为实际独掌政权的皇帝
events.note: Constantine removed the remaining Lekapenoi co-emperors and began his personal government after more than three decades of nominal imperial status.

events.label: Sponsored an unsuccessful expedition against Crete
events.labelCn: 发动对克里特岛但未成功的远征
events.note: A major expedition intended to recover Muslim-held Crete failed, although eastern frontier warfare later produced gains.

events.label: Compiled imperial knowledge for his son in De Administrando Imperio
events.labelCn: 为儿子编纂《帝国行政论》
events.note: During his personal reign Constantine sponsored and authored encyclopedic works on diplomacy, peoples, provinces and court ceremony; the exact composition dates span several years.

events.label: Received Olga of Kyiv at Constantinople
events.labelCn: 在君士坦丁堡接待基辅的奥尔加
events.note: Olga's famous visit formed part of Constantine's northern diplomacy and later Christian memory, though the exact relationship between the visit and her baptism remains debated.

events.label: Died and was succeeded by Romanos II
events.labelCn: 去世，由罗曼努斯二世继位
events.note: Constantine died in Constantinople after fourteen years of personal government; later poisoning rumors are not securely established.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, ch. 'Constantine VII, Porphyrogennetos [913–959]' (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Constantine VII, De Administrando Imperio, ed. Moravcsik/Jenkins; Prosopographie der mittelbyzantinischen Zeit; Larousse biography; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Constantine VII was the legitimate Macedonian emperor from childhood but spent 913–945 under regents and then Romanos I's dominant co-rule. His personal reign from 945 is especially important for court culture, scholarship, diplomacy and the preservation of Byzantine administrative knowledge.

Unlinked family: mother: Zoe Karbonopsina; spouse: Helena Lekapene; child: Theodora, wife of John I Tzimiskes; child: Zoe; child: Agatha; child: Theophano; child: Anna

fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝罗曼努斯二世
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor by Constantine VII
events.labelCn: 由君士坦丁七世加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Romanos was raised to co-emperor as his father's dynastic heir.

events.label: Married Theophano
events.labelCn: 迎娶狄奥法诺
events.note: Romanos chose Anastaso, who took the imperial name Theophano, after the death of his first child-bride Bertha-Eudokia.

events.label: Succeeded Constantine VII as senior emperor
events.labelCn: 继承君士坦丁七世成为主要皇帝
events.note: Romanos became sole senior ruler after his father's death.

events.label: Recovered Crete through Nikephoros Phokas
events.labelCn: 通过尼基弗鲁斯·福卡斯收复克里特岛
events.note: The expedition led by Nikephoros Phokas captured Chandax and restored Byzantine control of Crete after more than a century.

events.label: Died suddenly at a young age
events.labelCn: 年轻时突然去世
events.note: Romanos died after a sudden illness following a hunting expedition. Poisoning by Theophano was rumored in later narratives but is not established.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Warren Treadgold, A History of the Byzantine State and Society; Anthony Kaldellis, Streams of Gold, Rivers of Blood; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Romanos II inherited the Macedonian throne directly from Constantine VII, while delegating much government to Joseph Bringas and military operations to the Phokas brothers. His early death left the child emperors Basil II and Constantine VIII under a succession of powerful adult protectors.

Unlinked family: mother: Helena Lekapene; spouse: Bertha-Eudokia of Provence; child: Helena; child: Anna Porphyrogenita

displayNameCn: 巴西尔二世“保加利亚人屠夫”
fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝巴西尔二世“保加利亚人屠夫”
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor as a child
events.labelCn: 幼年被加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Romanos II raised Basil to the imperial college, preserving the Macedonian succession.

events.label: Remained child emperor after Romanos II's death
events.labelCn: 罗曼努斯二世去世后仍为幼年共治皇帝
events.note: Basil and Constantine VIII retained imperial status while Theophano, Nikephoros II and later John I controlled government.

events.label: Became senior emperor with Constantine VIII
events.labelCn: 与君士坦丁八世共同成为马其顿王朝主要皇帝
events.note: John I Tzimiskes's death returned formal senior power to the sons of Romanos II, although Basil Lekapenos initially dominated administration.

events.label: Survived the first revolt of Bardas Skleros
events.labelCn: 镇压巴尔达斯·斯克莱罗斯第一次叛乱
events.note: The rebellion challenged the young Macedonian emperors; Bardas Phokas and Georgian support helped defeat Skleros.

events.label: Removed Basil Lekapenos and took personal control
events.labelCn: 清除巴西尔·莱卡佩诺斯并亲掌政权
events.note: Basil exiled the powerful parakoimomenos Basil Lekapenos and confiscated much of his property, ending the long dominance of palace regents.

events.label: Suffered defeat at the Gate of Trajan
events.labelCn: 在图拉真门战役遭到惨败
events.note: After an unsuccessful siege of Serdica, Basil's retreating army was ambushed by the Bulgarians, a disaster that encouraged renewed aristocratic rebellion.

events.label: Faced the rebellion of Bardas Phokas
events.labelCn: 面对巴尔达斯·福卡斯称帝叛乱
events.note: Bardas Phokas proclaimed himself emperor and gained support across much of Anatolia while Bardas Skleros also re-entered the struggle.

events.label: Allied with Vladimir of Kyiv in exchange for dynastic marriage
events.labelCn: 与基辅的弗拉基米尔结盟并安排王朝婚姻
events.note: Vladimir supplied a major Rus'-Varangian force and accepted baptism; Basil's sister Anna was married to him, linking military aid with the Christianization of Rus'.

events.label: Defeated Bardas Phokas at Abydos
events.labelCn: 在阿卑多斯击败巴尔达斯·福卡斯
events.note: Phokas died during the confrontation at Abydos, breaking the most dangerous military-aristocratic challenge to Basil's rule.

events.label: Strengthened measures against great landowners
events.labelCn: 强化限制大地产贵族的政策
events.note: Basil issued legislation designed to protect smallholders and recover property acquired by the dynatoi, reinforcing the fiscal and military base of the state.

events.label: Opened the sustained phase of conquest against Samuel's Bulgaria
events.labelCn: 展开针对萨穆伊尔保加利亚的持续征服
events.note: From the turn of the century Basil pursued repeated annual operations in the Balkans, gradually dismantling Samuel's territorial system.

events.label: Crushed the Bulgarian army at Kleidion
events.labelCn: 在克莱迪翁战役重创保加利亚军
events.note: The victory broke a major Bulgarian field army. Later accounts famously describe the mass blinding of captives, but the scale of that punishment is debated.

events.label: Completed the conquest of the First Bulgarian Empire
events.labelCn: 完成对第一保加利亚帝国的征服
events.note: After the collapse of Bulgarian resistance, Basil incorporated the Bulgarian lands while preserving important local ecclesiastical and fiscal arrangements.

events.label: Forced Georgia to cede disputed frontier lands
events.labelCn: 迫使格鲁吉亚割让争议边疆领地
events.note: War with George I of Georgia ended with a settlement transferring Tao and other southwestern territories to Byzantine control.

events.label: Died while preparing another expedition
events.labelCn: 筹备新一轮远征时去世
events.note: Basil died in Constantinople after nearly half a century of effective senior rule. His brother Constantine VIII succeeded as sole emperor.

sourceNote: Catherine Holmes, Basil II and the Governance of Empire (976–1025), Oxford Studies in Byzantium; John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, ch. 'Basil II and Constantine VIII [976–1025]' (Cambridge); Anthony Kaldellis, Streams of Gold, Rivers of Blood; Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; The Cambridge History of the Byzantine Empire; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes: Basil II transformed a vulnerable child-emperor regime into the strongest Byzantine monarchy of the Middle Byzantine period. He defeated aristocratic rebellions, destroyed the Bulgarian imperial state, extended power in the Caucasus and left the empire territorially dominant, while Constantine VIII remained a largely inactive co-emperor.

fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝君士坦丁八世
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Was crowned co-emperor as a child
events.labelCn: 幼年被加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: Romanos II crowned his younger son Constantine, who then remained a nominal emperor under several senior rulers.

events.label: Became co-ruler with Basil II after John I's death
events.labelCn: 约翰一世去世后与巴西尔二世共同成为马其顿王朝皇帝
events.note: Constantine shared the imperial title with Basil II but took little part in government or warfare.

events.label: Became sole emperor after Basil II's death
events.labelCn: 巴西尔二世去世后成为唯一皇帝
events.note: After more than sixty years as a nominal co-emperor, Constantine became sole ruler.

events.label: Arranged Zoe's marriage to Romanos Argyros
events.labelCn: 安排女儿佐伊与罗曼努斯·阿尔吉罗斯成婚
events.note: With no surviving sons, Constantine used Zoe's marriage to secure a successor; Romanos was compelled to leave his previous wife.

events.label: Died and left the throne to Zoe and Romanos III
events.labelCn: 去世，将皇位留给佐伊与罗曼努斯三世
events.note: Constantine died shortly after arranging the marriage that carried Macedonian dynastic legitimacy into Romanos III's reign.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, ch. 'Basil II and Constantine VIII [976–1025]' and subsequent chapters (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Michael Psellos, Chronographia; Anthony Kaldellis, Streams of Gold, Rivers of Blood; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Constantine VIII was a crowned emperor from childhood but exercised almost no independent authority until Basil II died in 1025. His lack of sons made the marriages and dynastic status of daughters Zoe and Theodora central to the next three decades of imperial succession.

fullNameCn: 拜占庭女皇佐伊·紫衣贵族
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

titles.title: Augusta and dynastic co-ruler
titles.titleCn: 奥古斯塔兼王朝共治者

events.label: Set out for a proposed marriage to Otto III before his death
events.labelCn: 因拟与奥托三世联姻启程，但对方先行去世
events.note: Zoe was selected as a Byzantine bride for Otto III and reached southern Italy only to learn that the western emperor had died.

events.label: Married Romanos Argyros to secure the succession
events.labelCn: 为确保皇位继承与罗曼努斯·阿尔吉罗斯结婚
events.note: Constantine VIII chose Romanos as Zoe's husband at the end of his life, making the marriage the bridge from the male Macedonian line.

events.label: Became Augusta and dynastic co-ruler
events.labelCn: 成为奥古斯塔并成为王朝共治者
events.note: After Constantine VIII's death, Zoe's porphyrogenita status supplied the central dynastic legitimacy of Romanos III's reign.

events.label: Married Michael IV after Romanos III's death
events.labelCn: 罗曼努斯三世死后迎娶米海尔四世
events.note: Zoe married Michael the Paphlagonian immediately after Romanos III's suspicious death and raised him to imperial status.

events.label: Adopted Michael V as her heir
events.labelCn: 收养米海尔五世作为继承人
events.note: The adoption was intended to preserve continuity after the failing health of Michael IV, but Michael V soon attempted to remove Zoe.

events.label: Was exiled by Michael V and restored by a popular revolt
events.labelCn: 被米海尔五世流放后因民众起义复位
events.note: Michael V's attack on Zoe's status provoked a Constantinopolitan uprising that restored her and also elevated her sister Theodora.

events.label: Ruled jointly with Theodora
events.labelCn: 与狄奥多拉共同统治
events.note: For roughly seven weeks the sisters appeared as reigning empresses, with Zoe senior in ceremonial precedence.

events.label: Married Constantine IX Monomachos
events.labelCn: 第三次结婚，迎娶君士坦丁九世·莫诺马科斯
events.note: Zoe's third marriage transferred day-to-day imperial leadership to Constantine IX while Zoe and Theodora retained their imperial titles.

events.label: Died in Constantinople
events.labelCn: 在君士坦丁堡去世
events.note: Zoe died without biological children, leaving Theodora as the last surviving porphyrogenita of Constantine VIII's line.

sourceNote: Lynda Garland, Byzantine Empresses: Women and Power in Byzantium, AD 527–1204; Michael Psellos, Chronographia; John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Encyclopedia.com biographical entry on Zoe Porphyrogenita; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Zoe was not simply a consort: as Constantine VIII's porphyrogenita daughter she was the dynastic source through which three husbands obtained imperial legitimacy, and in 1042 she briefly ruled directly with Theodora. The Macedonian succession after 1028 is therefore best modeled around Zoe's continuing imperial status rather than as three unrelated male dynasties.

displayNameCn: 狄奥多拉·紫衣贵族女皇
fullNameCn: 拜占庭女皇狄奥多拉·紫衣贵族
birthPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Refused the proposed marriage to Romanos Argyros
events.labelCn: 拒绝与罗曼努斯·阿尔吉罗斯的拟议婚姻
events.note: Theodora objected to the proposed match on canonical and kinship grounds, after which Constantine VIII selected Zoe instead.

events.label: Was confined to monastic life after court conspiracies
events.labelCn: 因宫廷阴谋被迫进入修道院
events.note: Zoe's government treated Theodora as a potential dynastic focus for opposition and eventually removed her to the Petrion monastery.

events.label: Was proclaimed co-empress during the uprising against Michael V
events.labelCn: 反对米海尔五世的起义中被拥立为共治女皇
events.note: The Constantinopolitan populace and political elite insisted on restoring the second Macedonian princess alongside Zoe.

events.label: Ruled jointly with Zoe
events.labelCn: 与佐伊共同执政
events.note: The two sisters presided over the Senate, audiences and corrective administration until Zoe chose another husband.

events.label: Assumed sole rule after Constantine IX's death
events.labelCn: 君士坦丁九世死后开始单独统治
events.note: Theodora returned from political retirement and governed in her own name, becoming the last sovereign of the Macedonian dynasty.

events.label: Approved Michael VI as successor during her final illness
events.labelCn: 临终前认可米海尔六世为继承人
events.note: The court around Theodora secured the accession of the elderly bureaucrat Michael Bringas; the degree of Theodora's conscious approval was later disputed.

events.label: Died as the last Macedonian sovereign
events.labelCn: 作为马其顿王朝最后一位统治者去世
events.note: Theodora's death ended the direct ruling line descending from Basil I's dynasty.

sourceNote: Lynda Garland, Byzantine Empresses: Women and Power in Byzantium, AD 527–1204; Michael Psellos, Chronographia; John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History (Cambridge); Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Theodora was Zoe's sister and the final ruling member of the Macedonian dynasty. She briefly co-ruled directly with Zoe in 1042, retained imperial rank under Constantine IX, and returned to sole effective rule in 1055–1056.

notes: Daughter of Constantine VII, Theodora married John I Tzimiskes after his accession. The union made the military emperor the brother-in-law of Basil II and Constantine VIII, reinforcing his position without displacing the Macedonian co-emperors. Her later life is poorly documented.
